chapters.title: John sees the risen Christ among seven candlesticks

parts.text: The revelation of Jesus Christ is given to show his servants things that must shortly come to pass, with a blessing for those who read, hear, and keep it. John greets seven churches in Asia and praises Jesus, who washed them from their sins in his blood. Christ comes with clouds, every eye will see him, and the kindreds of the earth will mourn.

On Patmos for God’s word and Jesus’ testimony, John hears a command to write what he sees. Among seven golden candlesticks he sees one like the Son of man in overwhelming glory. Jesus reassures him as the living one who was dead and holds the keys of hell and death. He identifies the stars as the churches’ angels and the candlesticks as the churches.

chapters.title: Messages to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, and Thyatira

parts.text: Ephesus is commended for labour, patience, and exposing false apostles, but must repent of leaving its first love. The overcomer is promised the tree of life. Smyrna is poor yet spiritually rich and faces imprisonment and ten days of tribulation. Christ calls for faithfulness unto death, promising a crown of life and freedom from the second death.

Pergamos holds Christ’s name amid persecution but tolerates teaching associated with Balaam and the Nicolaitans. It must repent; the overcomer is promised hidden manna and a white stone with a new name. Thyatira’s growing service is praised, but Jezebel’s teaching leads servants into fornication and idolatry. Judgment threatens the unrepentant. The faithful must hold fast until Christ comes; those overcoming and keeping his works receive authority over nations and the morning star.

chapters.title: Messages to Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea

parts.text: Sardis has a reputation for life but is dead. It must watch, strengthen what remains, remember, and repent. The undefiled will walk with Christ in white, and the overcomer’s name is confessed before the Father. Philadelphia, though weak, has kept Christ’s word and receives an open door. Christ promises vindication and preservation from the worldwide hour of temptation. It must hold fast; the overcomer receives a lasting place and God’s name.

Laodicea’s lukewarmness and self-satisfied wealth hide its poverty, blindness, and nakedness. Christ counsels it to obtain true riches, clothing, and sight from him. His rebuke expresses love and calls for zealous repentance. He offers fellowship to whoever opens to his voice, and a place on his throne to the overcomer.

chapters.title: Worship before the throne in heaven

parts.text: John sees an open door in heaven and is called to behold things that must be hereafter. In the Spirit he sees a throne surrounded by a rainbow and twenty-four crowned elders dressed in white. Lightning, thunder, and voices proceed from the throne. Seven burning lamps are identified as God’s seven Spirits, and a sea like crystal lies before it.

Four living creatures, described with different faces and full of eyes, continually proclaim the holiness of the everlasting Lord God Almighty. As they give him glory, the elders fall down, cast their crowns before his throne, and worship. They declare him worthy of glory, honour, and power because he created all things for his pleasure.

chapters.title: The Lamb is worthy to open the sealed book

parts.text: John sees a book sealed with seven seals in the right hand of the one on the throne. No one is found worthy to open it, and John weeps until an elder announces that the Lion of Juda, the Root of David, has prevailed. John sees a Lamb standing as though slain, with seven horns and seven eyes, identified as God’s seven Spirits. The Lamb takes the book.

The living creatures and elders worship with harps and golden vessels holding the saints’ prayers. Their new song praises the Lamb for redeeming them by his blood from every nation and making them kings and priests. Innumerable angels proclaim his worthiness, and every creature joins in blessing the one on the throne and the Lamb.

chapters.title: The Lamb opens the first six seals

parts.text: The first four seals reveal riders on white, red, black, and pale horses. They bring conquest, the removal of peace, measured food at stated prices, and death. The fourth rider is named Death, with Hell following; they receive power over a fourth of the earth to kill by sword, hunger, death, and wild beasts.

At the fifth seal, souls slain for God’s word ask when their blood will be avenged. Given white robes, they must rest until their fellow servants also face death. The sixth seal brings a great earthquake, a darkened sun, a bloodlike moon, falling stars, and the removal of heaven like a rolled scroll. All ranks of people hide, declaring that the great day of the Lamb’s wrath has come.

chapters.title: Israel’s servants are sealed and a multitude worships

parts.text: Four angels restrain the earth’s winds. Another angel commands that the earth, sea, and trees must not be harmed until God’s servants are sealed in their foreheads. John hears their number: 144,000, with twelve thousand from each of twelve named tribes of Israel.

John then sees an innumerable multitude from every nation before the throne and the Lamb, wearing white robes and holding palms. They praise God for salvation while heaven joins in worship. An elder explains that they came out of great tribulation and washed their robes in the Lamb’s blood. They serve God in his temple under his dwelling presence, free from hunger, thirst, and scorching heat. The Lamb leads them to living waters, and God wipes away their tears.

chapters.title: The seventh seal and the first four trumpets

parts.text: Opening the seventh seal brings about half an hour of silence in heaven. Seven angels receive trumpets. Another angel offers incense with the prayers of all saints at the golden altar, then casts fire from the altar onto the earth. Voices, thunder, lightning, and an earthquake follow as the trumpet angels prepare to sound.

The first trumpet brings hail and fire mixed with blood, burning a third of the trees and all green grass. The second brings something like a burning mountain into the sea, destroying a third of its life and ships. The star Wormwood makes a third of the waters bitter at the third trumpet. The fourth darkens a third of the heavenly lights. An angel announces three woes with the remaining trumpets.

chapters.title: Locust torment and a deadly mounted army

parts.text: At the fifth trumpet, a fallen star receives the key to the bottomless pit and opens it. Smoke darkens the air, and locusts with terrifying features emerge under their king, Abaddon or Apollyon. They may torment people lacking God’s seal for five months but may neither kill them nor harm vegetation. People seek death without finding it. This is the first woe.

The sixth trumpet releases four angels bound at the Euphrates, prepared to kill a third of mankind. John hears the number of a mounted army: two hundred thousand thousand. Their horses kill with fire, smoke, and brimstone from their mouths and injure with serpentlike tails. The survivors still refuse to repent of idolatry, murders, sorceries, fornication, or thefts.

chapters.title: John eats the little book and must prophesy again

parts.text: A mighty angel descends with an open little book, standing on the sea and earth. At his cry, seven thunders speak, but John is forbidden to write their words. The angel swears by the eternal Creator that there should be time no longer, and that in the days when the seventh angel begins sounding, God’s mystery will be finished as declared to the prophets.

John is told to take and eat the little book. The angel warns that it will be sweet in his mouth but bitter in his belly. John eats it and experiences both, just as he was told. He must prophesy again before many peoples, nations, tongues, and kings.

chapters.title: Two witnesses testify and the seventh trumpet sounds

parts.text: John must measure the temple, altar, and worshippers but leave the outer court, given to the Gentiles who tread the holy city for forty-two months. Two witnesses prophesy for 1,260 days with power over their enemies and over plagues. When their testimony is finished, the beast from the bottomless pit kills them. Their bodies lie in the city where the Lord was crucified while the earth’s inhabitants celebrate.

After three and a half days, God raises the witnesses and calls them into heaven. An earthquake destroys a tenth of the city and kills seven thousand; survivors glorify God. The second woe passes. At the seventh trumpet, heaven announces the Lord’s everlasting kingdom and the time for judgment and reward. God’s heavenly temple opens, revealing the ark amid powerful signs.

chapters.title: The dragon opposes the woman and her seed

parts.text: John sees a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon beneath her feet and twelve stars on her head. A great red dragon waits to devour her child. The male child, destined to rule all nations with a rod of iron, is caught up to God’s throne. The woman flees to a wilderness place prepared by God, where she is fed for 1,260 days.

Michael and his angels defeat the dragon, identified as the Devil and Satan, and cast him and his angels to earth. Heaven celebrates, but earth is warned of his wrath. The dragon persecutes the woman, who receives protection in the wilderness for a time, times, and half a time. Frustrated, he wars against her remaining seed, who keep God’s commandments and Jesus’ testimony.

chapters.title: Two beasts demand worship and impose a mark

parts.text: A beast rises from the sea with seven heads and ten horns, receiving authority from the dragon. A healed deadly wound brings worldwide wonder and worship. For forty-two months it speaks blasphemies, wars against the saints, and exercises authority over nations. Those not written in the Lamb’s book of life worship it. The passage calls for the saints’ patience and faith.

Another beast rises from the earth, with lamb-like horns but a dragon’s speech. It performs wonders, promotes worship of the first beast, and gives life to its image. Refusal to worship the image brings death. It imposes a mark in the right hand or forehead, restricting buying and selling to those with the mark, name, or number. The beast’s number is 666.

chapters.title: The Lamb’s followers, angelic warnings, and harvests

parts.text: The Lamb stands on mount Sion with 144,000 bearing his Father’s name. Redeemed as firstfruits, they follow him and are described as virgins without deceit or fault. Angels announce the everlasting gospel and the arrival of judgment, declare Babylon fallen, and warn of unending torment for worshipping the beast and receiving its mark. The saints are characterized by endurance, obedience, and faith in Jesus. Those dying in the Lord are blessed with rest.

John sees one like the Son of man on a white cloud, crowned and holding a sickle. At an angel’s call, he reaps the earth’s ripe harvest. Another angel gathers its vine into the winepress of God’s wrath. Trodden outside the city, it produces blood reaching the horses’ bridles for 1,600 furlongs.

chapters.title: Seven angels receive the last plagues

parts.text: John sees seven angels with seven last plagues, in which God’s wrath is filled up. Those victorious over the beast, its image, mark, and number stand on a sea like glass mixed with fire, holding God’s harps. They sing the song of Moses and the Lamb, praising God’s mighty works, just ways, and holiness. All nations will worship as his judgments are revealed.

The heavenly temple opens, and the seven angels emerge in pure white linen with golden girdles. One of the living creatures gives them seven golden vials full of God’s wrath. Smoke from God’s glory and power fills the temple, preventing anyone from entering until the seven plagues are completed.

chapters.title: Seven vials pour out God’s wrath

parts.text: The seven angels are commanded to pour out God’s wrath. The first vial brings grievous sores on the beast’s worshippers. The second turns the sea to blood, killing every living soul in it; the third turns rivers and springs to blood. Heaven declares this just repayment for shedding the saints’ blood. The fourth brings scorching heat, and the fifth darkens the beast’s kingdom. Those afflicted blaspheme rather than repent.

The sixth dries the Euphrates for eastern kings. Unclean spirits gather the world’s kings to battle at Armageddon, while a warning calls for watchfulness. The seventh brings a declaration of completion, an unprecedented earthquake, the fall of cities, and judgment on Babylon. Islands and mountains disappear, and enormous hail provokes further blasphemy.

chapters.title: The woman, the beast, and the ten kings explained

parts.text: An angel shows John the judgment of the great whore. In the wilderness he sees a richly dressed woman riding a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns. Named Babylon the Great, she is drunk with the blood of saints and Jesus’ martyrs. The angel explains that the beast was, is not, and will ascend from the bottomless pit before going to destruction.

The heads represent seven mountains, and the explanation also describes seven kings and the beast as an eighth. Ten horns are kings who briefly receive authority and support the beast. They war against the Lamb, who defeats them. The waters represent peoples and nations; the woman is the great city reigning over earthly kings. The horns turn against and destroy her, fulfilling God’s purpose.

chapters.title: Babylon falls and her trading partners mourn

parts.text: An angel announces Babylon’s fall and describes her as a dwelling for devils and unclean spirits. Nations, kings, and merchants have shared in her corruption and luxury. A heavenly voice calls God’s people to leave her, avoiding participation in her sins and plagues. Her proud confidence gives way to death, mourning, famine, and burning under God’s judgment.

Kings, merchants, and seafarers mourn from a distance as her wealth and commerce vanish. Their goods include luxuries, necessities, slaves, and human souls. Heaven, apostles, and prophets are told to rejoice because God has avenged them. An angel throws a great stone into the sea to portray Babylon’s irreversible overthrow. Music, trades, light, and marriage celebrations cease in the city guilty of deception and bloodshed.

chapters.title: Heaven rejoices and the King defeats the beast

parts.text: Heaven praises God for judging the great whore and avenging his servants. The multitude celebrates the Lord’s reign and the marriage of the Lamb. His wife is clothed in fine linen, explained as the righteousness of saints, and those invited to the marriage supper are blessed. When John attempts to worship the messenger, he is told to worship God.

Heaven opens to reveal a white-horse rider called Faithful and True, the Word of God, and King of kings and Lord of lords. Heavenly armies follow him as he judges the nations. Birds are summoned to feast on the defeated. The beast and false prophet are captured and cast alive into the lake of fire. Their army is slain by the sword proceeding from the rider’s mouth.

chapters.title: A thousand-year reign, Satan’s end, and final judgment

parts.text: An angel binds Satan in the bottomless pit for a thousand years so that he cannot deceive the nations until his brief release afterward. John sees thrones and those beheaded for Jesus’ testimony who refused the beast’s worship and mark. They live and reign with Christ a thousand years. Those sharing the first resurrection are blessed, beyond the second death’s power, while the rest of the dead await the thousand years’ completion.

Released afterward, Satan gathers Gog and Magog against the saints and beloved city. Fire from God consumes them, and the devil enters the lake of fire. Before a great white throne, the dead are judged according to their works. Death and hell enter the lake of fire, as does everyone absent from the book of life.

chapters.title: A new creation and the holy city

parts.text: John sees a new heaven and earth, with no more sea, and new Jerusalem descending from God. God dwells with his people, removing tears, death, sorrow, and pain. He makes all things new, offers the water of life freely, and promises the overcomer an inheritance as his son. The unbelieving and wicked instead face the second death in the lake of fire.

An angel shows John the bride, the Lamb’s wife, as the holy city descending in God’s glory. Its gates bear Israel’s tribes’ names and its foundations the apostles’ names. Its equal dimensions, precious stones, gold, and pearl gates display its splendour. God and the Lamb are its temple and light. Saved nations walk in that light, and only those in the Lamb’s book of life enter.

chapters.title: The water of life and the promise of Christ’s coming

parts.text: A river of life flows from God’s and the Lamb’s throne beside the tree of life, whose fruit appears monthly and whose leaves heal the nations. The curse and night are gone. God’s servants see his face, bear his name, and reign forever. The sayings are declared faithful and true, and those keeping the prophecy are blessed. John again attempts to worship the angel and is directed to worship God.

The prophecy must remain unsealed because the time is near. Jesus announces his coming with reward according to each person’s work. Obedient people enter the city; the wicked remain outside. The Spirit and bride invite the thirsty to take life’s water freely. Warnings forbid adding to or taking from the prophecy. John answers Christ’s promised coming with prayer and closes with grace.
